messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
I’d like the coffee working again without a fight. I can help coordinate, but I can’t take on chasing everyone or deciding for you both.

I’d be happiest with a simpler machine that doesn’t need much upkeep. The old one has a lot of history for B, so I’d hope we can find an option that feels manageable without a big repair or cleaning commitment.

I want the old machine repaired and kept. A simpler machine might be easier, but I’d rather not replace it. A good outcome is getting it working reliably without turning this into a big time-consuming project; I can only manage it in small slots.
Yes, that fits. I’d just add that I’d prefer not to leave anyone with ongoing upkeep to manage.
Yes, that fits. I’d add that I want it working reliably—not just patched up so it leaks again next week.
Yes, that fits. I don’t want to be responsible for chasing everyone or handling the repair.

I’m a little hesitant about making replacement depend on a repair attempt first. I’d prefer we consider a simpler, low-upkeep machine now too, and keep any repair decision from turning into a long process.
Both in sequence could work, but don’t assume one professional repair will make it reliable. I’d need to know the cost and what the repairer can actually guarantee before agreeing.
The sequence seems reasonable, but I don’t know whether repair is feasible or affordable. I can’t take on arranging or chasing it.
That sounds manageable if B or someone else is willing to make the call and it stays to one quick step. I wouldn’t be able to take on follow-up or coordination.
I can make one call when I have a slot, but I can’t promise a short deadline or take on chasing after it. If it turns into more than one call, someone else needs to handle it.
Yes, I’m comfortable with A or B making the calls. I can’t take that on myself.
Yes, that’s a real concern. Maybe: “I need to be free of follow-up and coordination, and no one should be left carrying it alone.”
Yes, that’s accurate as a limit, not a need. I can make one call when I have time; I can’t promise a deadline or handle follow-up.
